scope: Additional source research prompted by parent; no compiler/test/integral/runtime launch. Not a revision of frozen build protocol or an exemption from current exact archive-map gate.
finding: The current probe uses -C lto=thin without linker-plugin-lto. are_upstream_rust_objects_already_included returns true; add_static_crate removes metadata and Rust object archive members. A residual native archive may be emitted under temporary directory; empty pure Rust residual archives are not linked. Therefore original source rlib absolute paths are not guaranteed to appear in final linker map even when exactly the intended rlibs supplied all upstream IR. The current exact-original-four-path map gate can conservatively fail at its first optimized probe.
implication: Prior source review established coherent explicit dependency chain and conservative failure behavior; it did not establish an actual optimized linker map. Existing map gate must remain unchanged for active attempt, preserve first terminal evidence and all artifacts, and do not execute its unqualified binary. Any new build/admission strategy requires a separate reviewed protocol and root resource coordination.
possible_future_strategies: Use matched optimized probes with LTO off if that is the desired benchmark profile, preserving direct original archive-map evidence; this changes the final optimization profile and requires a new proposal and numerical qualification.

For intended ThinLTO, develop a separately reviewed provenance proof of pre-LTO compiler input selection (e.g. exact hash-bound fresh externs plus traced successful archive opens and a clean dependency search directory excluding stale Symbolica/OneLoop/IREGI copies), while retaining final link map for transformed native objects. This is a future design, not permission to relax current map admission.
